name: Contradictory Persistent CIDR Constraints
research_question: Does the CSP evaluator return UNSAT when two hops impose disjoint CIDR constraints under a static-origin assumption?

transition_constraints.rationale: Static origin assumption: attacker operates from fixed origin across sequential role assumptions.

formal_rationale: The first hop imposes 10.0.0.0/8 and the second hop imposes 192.168.0.0/16. These CIDRs are disjoint (10.0.0.0/8 covers 10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255, while 192.168.0.0/16 covers 192.168.0.0-192.168.255.255). Under the static-origin assumption (EQUAL transition), the constraint system requires a single IP address to simultaneously belong to both CIDRs. Since these CIDRs have no overlap, no such IP exists. The constraint system is unsatisfiable. The evaluator must return UNSAT at hop 2 where the contradiction is introduced.
falsification_criteria: The feasibility hypothesis is falsified if the evaluator outputs SAT (failing to detect the disjoint CIDR contradiction) or UNKNOWN (failing to evaluate the complete chain under static origin). The evaluator must detect the contradiction specifically at hop 2.
